valid_fixes: Restore FRIEND_TABLE to !Ref FriendTable in the template AND restore the exception handler in request-state-handler/index.py to re-raise non-ConditionalCheckFailed errors
invalid_patches: Restore only FRIEND_TABLE env var without fixing the exception swallow — leaves a latent reliability defect where any future DynamoDB error is silently lost
Fix only the exception handler without correcting FRIEND_TABLE — causes Lambda errors and DLQ routing but the Pending record is still never written
optimal_diagnostic_path: ace_get_log_tail(FunctionName=<stack>-request-state-handler) → invocations complete without error despite no Pending record written
ace_check_queue_depth(QueueUrl=<state-handler-dlq-url>) → depth 0, confirming no failures were routed to DLQ
observable_symptom: RequestStateHandlerFunction logs show successful invocations with no errors. The DLQ depth remains zero. The receiver-side Pending record never appears in the table despite the requester-side Requested record existing. The system presents no observable error signal at any layer.
root_cause: FRIEND_TABLE env var is set to the hardcoded string 'friend-table' (a non-existent table) instead of the stack-namespaced table name. Every put_item call raises ResourceNotFoundException. The exception handler in _create_pending uses bare 'except ClientError: pass', swallowing all ClientError subclasses including ResourceNotFoundException. The handler returns batchItemFailures: [], Lambda marks the batch successful, and no error reaches the DLQ or CloudWatch error metrics.
